findings.title: Unused local helper `_handle_regex_match` left behind in `parametrize_w_experiments`
findings.body: In `Parameterizer.parametrize_w_experiments`, removing `ParameterizationRegexExperiment` deleted the only call to the nested `_handle_regex_match` helper, leaving `_handle_regex_match` (lines 335-343) defined on every call to `parametrize_w_experiments` but never referenced.

findings.title: `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` fail when `age=0` or `timestamp=0`
findings.body: `BrowserReportSerializer.validate_timestamp` checks `if self.initial_data.get("age"):` and `validate_age` checks `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp"):`. Because `0` is falsy in Python and `0` is a valid non-negative value for both `age` (a report delivered immediately has `age: 0` per the Reporting API spec) and `timestamp` (`min_value=0`), a payload containing both `timestamp` and `age: 0` (or `age` and `timestamp: 0`) bypasses the mutual-exclusion check. Additionally, neither `age` nor `timestamp` is required, so a report with neither field set is accepted. Check `"age" in self.initial_data` / `self.initial_data.get("age") is not None` (and similarly for `timestamp`), or validate mutual exclusion and presence in `validate()`.

findings.title: `fetch_error_details` pairs `error_ids` with `events.values()` instead of matching by `node_id`
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids = [Event.generate_node_id(project_id, event_id=id) for id in error_ids]`, calls `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)`, and then iterates `for event_id, data in zip(error_ids, events.values())`. `nodestore.get_multi` returns a dict mapping `node_id -> data` whose keys are not guaranteed to be in the same order as `node_ids` or to include missing keys (depending on the nodestore backend implementation). Zipping `error_ids` with `events.values()` can therefore associate an `event_id` with the wrong event's payload or drop/shift entries when some nodes are missing or when `error_ids` contains duplicates. Look up each node via `events.get(node_id)` while iterating `(error_id, node_id)` pairs.

findings.title: `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` are only filtered out when a search query is entered
findings.body: In `Attributes`, `sortedAndFilteredAttributes` returns `sorted` directly when `!searchQuery.trim()` (lines 61-63), and only applies `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name)` inside the `filter` branch when `searchQuery` is non-empty (lines 65-69). As a result, `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` are displayed in the attributes tree by default and only disappear once the user types into the search box. Filter out `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` before checking `searchQuery`.

findings.title: Replacing `FlexBox` with `<Flex direction="column" flex={1}>` drops `height: 100%` on waterfall container
findings.body: `TraceWaterfall` previously rendered `<FlexBox>` which had `display: flex; flex-grow: 1; flex-direction: column; height: 100%;`. It was replaced with `<Flex direction="column" flex={1}>`, which does not set `height: 100%` (and sets `flex: 1` instead of `flex-grow: 1`). When `TraceWaterfall`'s parent is not a flex column container, losing `height: 100%` causes the waterfall container to collapse instead of filling its parent's height.
